d: Explore how stylesheets let you declare and globally apply overrides to UI instance properties.
h:
UI styling is a Roblox solution to stylesheets, similar to CSS, that lets you declare and globally apply overrides to UI instance properties. This engine‑level support is the foundation for the Style Editor and the end‑to‑end token pipeline.

Concepts

Style rules (part of a StyleSheet) apply to every instance that matches the rule's Selector definition to match characteristics such as class name, instance name, and hierarchy relationships. See the Selector documentation for details.

Style tokens, defined through attributes of a token StyleSheet, represent UI property variables that can be used across styles and components, for example a common color for a Frame.BackgroundColor3, TextLabel.TextColor3, and UIStroke.Color. Tokens are comparable to CSS variables.

Style themes, configured through attributes of a theme StyleSheet, consist of sets of specific tokens that can be swapped, for example color tokens that define a "light" and "dark" theme. Related themes must have the same set of tokens to work correctly.

Style queries allow you to apply styles conditionally based on the UI's context or environment. These are comparable to CSS container queries and media queries, enabling UI to adapt to screen size, input types, or user accessibility settings.

Rule propagation

A StyleLink instance links a StyleSheet and its associated rules to a parent ScreenGui and all of the GuiObjects within it. Only one StyleSheet can apply to a given tree.

Selector definitions

At a high level, instance matching and modification via a rule's Selector definition operates through:

  • Roblox class selectors which target all instances of a given GuiObject class, for example Frame, ImageLabel, TextButton, etc.
  • Instance tags applied to specific UI objects through CollectionService.
  • Instance name selection according to the value of the UI object's Instance.Name.
  • Instance modifiers, similar to CSS pseudo-elements, applied through phantom UIComponents such as UICorner or UIStroke.
  • GuiObject state selectors, similar to CSS pseudo-class selectors, which correspond to one of the four GuiState enum values such as Hover.
  • Roblox query selectors, similar to CSS container and media queries, which use the @ prefix to apply styles only while a StyleQuery instance or pseudo‑instance with the same name is active.

The following setup shows how size and color tokens, a theme, and a class selector of "Frame" produce a magenta Frame of size 200×200 pixels.

Code Equivalent

UI Class Selector

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local screenGui = script.Parent

-- Tokens
local tokens = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
tokens.Name = "Tokens"
tokens.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
tokens:SetAttribute("SquareS", UDim2.fromOffset(50, 50))
tokens:SetAttribute("SquareM", UDim2.fromOffset(100, 100))
tokens:SetAttribute("SquareL", UDim2.fromOffset(200, 200))
tokens:SetAttribute("Fit", UDim2.fromScale(1, 1))
tokens:SetAttribute("Magenta", Color3.fromHex("FF0099"))
tokens:SetAttribute("Gold", Color3.fromHex("FFCC00"))
tokens:SetAttribute("Aqua", Color3.fromHex("0093F0"))

-- ThemeA
local themeA = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
themeA.Name = "ThemeA"
themeA.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local tokensDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
tokensDerive.StyleSheet = tokens  -- Derive global tokens
tokensDerive.Parent = themeA
themeA:SetAttribute("FrameSize", "$SquareM")
themeA:SetAttribute("FrameColor", "$Aqua")

-- ThemeB
local themeB = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
themeB.Name = "ThemeB"
themeB.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local tokensDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
tokensDerive.StyleSheet = tokens  -- Derive global tokens
tokensDerive.Parent = themeB
themeB:SetAttribute("FrameSize", "$SquareL")
themeB:SetAttribute("FrameColor", "$Magenta")

-- DesignSheet
local designSheet = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
designSheet.Name = "DesignSheet"
designSheet.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local themeDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
themeDerive.StyleSheet = themeB  -- Derive from ThemeB
themeDerive.Parent = designSheet

-- Link DesignSheet to ScreenGui
local styleLink = Instance.new("StyleLink")
styleLink.StyleSheet = designSheet
styleLink.Parent = screenGui

-- Configure rule
local rule = Instance.new("StyleRule")
rule.Selector = "Frame"  -- Class selector
rule.Parent = designSheet

-- Set rule properties
rule:SetProperties({
    ["BackgroundColor3"] = "$FrameColor",
    ["Size"] = "$FrameSize",
    ["BorderSizePixel"] = 0
})

local frame = Instance.new("Frame")
frame.Parent = screenGui

This setup shows how size/color/font tokens, a theme, and a tag selector of ".ButtonPrimary" produces a gold button using the Oswald font at 32 pixels.

Code Equivalent

UI Tag Selector

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local screenGui = script.Parent

-- Tokens
local tokens = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
tokens.Name = "Tokens"
tokens.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
tokens:SetAttribute("Text24", 24)
tokens:SetAttribute("Text32", 32)
tokens:SetAttribute("Magenta", Color3.fromHex("FF0099"))
tokens:SetAttribute("Gold", Color3.fromHex("FFCC00"))
tokens:SetAttribute("Aqua", Color3.fromHex("0093F0"))
tokens:SetAttribute("DenkOne", Enum.Font.DenkOne)
tokens:SetAttribute("Oswald", Enum.Font.Oswald)

-- ThemeA
local themeA = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
themeA.Name = "ThemeA"
themeA.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local tokensDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
tokensDerive.StyleSheet = tokens  -- Derive global tokens
tokensDerive.Parent = themeA
themeA:SetAttribute("BackColor", "$Gold")
themeA:SetAttribute("TextSize", "$Text32")
themeA:SetAttribute("ButtonFont", "$Oswald")

-- ThemeB
local themeB = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
themeB.Name = "ThemeB"
themeB.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local tokensDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
tokensDerive.StyleSheet = tokens  -- Derive global tokens
tokensDerive.Parent = themeB
themeB:SetAttribute("BackColor", "$Aqua")
themeB:SetAttribute("TextSize", "$Text24")
themeB:SetAttribute("ButtonFont", "$DenkOne")

-- DesignSheet
local designSheet = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
designSheet.Name = "DesignSheet"
designSheet.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local themeDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
themeDerive.StyleSheet = themeA  -- Derive from ThemeA
themeDerive.Parent = designSheet

-- Link DesignSheet to ScreenGui
local styleLink = Instance.new("StyleLink")
styleLink.StyleSheet = designSheet
styleLink.Parent = screenGui

-- Configure rule
local rule = Instance.new("StyleRule")
rule.Selector = ".ButtonPrimary"  -- Tag selector
rule.Parent = designSheet

-- Set rule properties
rule:SetProperties({
    ["BackgroundColor3"] = "$BackColor",
    ["TextSize"] = "$TextSize",
    ["Font"] = "$ButtonFont",
    ["BorderSizePixel"] = 0
})

local menuButton = Instance.new("TextButton")
menuButton.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 44)
menuButton.Text = "Menu"
menuButton.Parent = screenGui
CollectionService:AddTag(menuButton, "ButtonPrimary")  -- Apply tag to button

This setup shows how tokens, a theme, a class selector of "Frame", and a nested UI modifier selector of "::UICorner" produce a 300×160 orange Frame with a UICorner modifier of 20 pixels.

Code Equivalent

UI Modifier Selector

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local screenGui = script.Parent

-- Tokens
local tokens = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
tokens.Name = "Tokens"
tokens.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
tokens:SetAttribute("RectS", UDim2.fromOffset(75, 40))
tokens:SetAttribute("RectM", UDim2.fromOffset(150, 80))
tokens:SetAttribute("RectL", UDim2.fromOffset(300, 160))
tokens:SetAttribute("Magenta", Color3.fromHex("FF0099"))
tokens:SetAttribute("Orange", Color3.fromHex("DD6030"))
tokens:SetAttribute("Radius20", UDim.new(0, 20))
tokens:SetAttribute("RadiusPill", UDim.new(0.5, 0))

-- ThemeA
local themeA = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
themeA.Name = "ThemeA"
themeA.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local tokensDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
tokensDerive.StyleSheet = tokens  -- Derive global tokens
tokensDerive.Parent = themeA
themeA:SetAttribute("FrameSize", "$RectM")
themeA:SetAttribute("FrameColor", "$Magenta")
themeA:SetAttribute("CornerRad", "$Radius20")

-- ThemeB
local themeB = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
themeB.Name = "ThemeB"
themeB.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local tokensDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
tokensDerive.StyleSheet = tokens  -- Derive global tokens
tokensDerive.Parent = themeB
themeB:SetAttribute("FrameSize", "$RectL")
themeB:SetAttribute("FrameColor", "$Orange")
themeB:SetAttribute("CornerRad", "$Radius20")

-- DesignSheet
local designSheet = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
designSheet.Name = "DesignSheet"
designSheet.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
local themeDerive = Instance.new("StyleDerive")
themeDerive.StyleSheet = themeB  -- Derive from ThemeB
themeDerive.Parent = designSheet

-- Link DesignSheet to ScreenGui
local styleLink = Instance.new("StyleLink")
styleLink.StyleSheet = designSheet
styleLink.Parent = screenGui

-- Configure rules
local frameRule = Instance.new("StyleRule")
frameRule.Selector = "Frame"  -- Class selector
frameRule.Parent = designSheet
local modifierRule = Instance.new("StyleRule")
modifierRule.Selector = "::UICorner"  -- UI modifier selector
modifierRule.Parent = frameRule

-- Set rule properties
frameRule:SetProperties({
    ["BackgroundColor3"] = "$FrameColor",
    ["Size"] = "$FrameSize",
    ["BorderSizePixel"] = 0
})
modifierRule:SetProperty("CornerRadius", "$CornerRad")

local frame = Instance.new("Frame")
frame.Parent = screenGui

Modified properties

Instance properties affected by styling are flagged with a ⚠ in the Properties window, and hovering over an affected property shows which style is influencing it. For example, if a style rule tells a tagged Frame to use an AnchorPoint of 0.5, 0.5, that object property will show the default value of 0, 0 but its actual AnchorPoint will use the rule's styled value.

When a default or styled property value is further modified for a specific UI object, it becomes bold to indicate an overridden value. For example — assuming a default AnchorPoint of 0, 0 — setting that property to 1, 1 for a specific instance reveals an override in bold:

For any overridden property value, you can right-click it in the Properties window and select Reset to Default to revert it to the styled value, or to the default property value if it hasn't been styled.

kid.simple: This page introduces UI styling, a way to set how your buttons, frames, and labels look from one central place instead of changing each one by hand. You write style rules inside a `StyleSheet`, and every matching UI object picks up those looks automatically. You can also save shared values like colors and sizes as tokens, and group tokens into themes such as light and dark. If your game has lots of menus, this saves tons of time and keeps everything matching.
kid.analogy: It is like a school uniform rule: instead of telling every student what to wear one by one, the school writes one rule, "all students wear a blue shirt", and everyone it applies to follows it. Change the rule to green, and everyone switches at once.
keyPoints: A `StyleSheet` holds style rules, and each `StyleRule` has a `Selector` that decides which UI objects it changes.
Selectors can match by class (like every `Frame`), by tag (like `.ButtonPrimary`), by name (like `#ModalFrame`), by state (like `:Hover`), or add modifiers (like `::UICorner`).
Tokens are named values stored as attributes on a `StyleSheet`, like a color called `Magenta`. Rules use them with a `$` in front, like `$Magenta`.
Themes are sets of the same token names with different values, so you can swap a whole look (for example light and dark) at once.
Style queries let styles apply only in certain situations, like small screens, a certain input type, or reduced motion turned on.
A `StyleLink` placed inside a `ScreenGui` connects one `StyleSheet` to that `ScreenGui` and everything inside it. Only one style sheet can apply to a given tree.
In the Properties window, a styled property shows a warning mark, and hovering it tells you which style is changing it.
If you set a property by hand on one object, it shows in bold as an override. Right-click it and choose Reset to Default to go back to the styled value.

terms.stylesheet: A container of style rules, like a recipe book of looks. In Roblox it is the `StyleSheet` instance.
terms.style rule: One instruction inside a style sheet, such as "all Frames are magenta and 200 by 200 pixels".
terms.selector: The text on a rule that says which objects it targets. `"Frame"` means every Frame, `".ButtonPrimary"` means objects tagged ButtonPrimary.
terms.token: A named, reusable value, like a variable for design. If token `Gold` is `#FFCC00`, any rule using `$Gold` gets that yellow color.
terms.theme: A group of tokens that can be swapped as a set. ThemeA might say `FrameColor` is aqua, ThemeB might say it is magenta.
terms.attribute: A custom labeled value you attach to any instance. Tokens are stored as attributes on a style sheet.
terms.derive: To inherit tokens and rules from another style sheet. A `StyleDerive` instance points one sheet at another to borrow from it.
terms.tag: A label you stick on an instance through `CollectionService`, so rules or scripts can find all objects with that label.
terms.modifier: An extra UI piece like `UICorner` (rounded corners) or `UIStroke` (outline). Styling can add a phantom one without you inserting it.
terms.phantom: Not really in the Explorer. A phantom `UICorner` acts like it is there because a rule says so, but you will not see it as a child.
terms.state: What is happening to a UI object right now. There are four `GuiState` values: `Idle`, `Hover`, `Press`, and `NonInteractable`.
terms.query: A condition, like "only on small screens". Query selectors start with `@`.
terms.override: A value you set directly on one object that wins over the styled value. It shows in bold.
terms.propagation: How a style spreads. A `StyleLink` on a `ScreenGui` spreads the sheet's rules to every UI object inside that ScreenGui.

example.title: Make every Frame magenta with one rule
example.place: LocalScript inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui
example.code:
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local screenGui = script.Parent

-- Create a style sheet to hold our rules and tokens
local sheet = Instance.new("StyleSheet")
sheet.Name = "DesignSheet"
sheet.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

-- Tokens are attributes on the sheet
sheet:SetAttribute("Magenta", Color3.fromHex("FF0099"))
sheet:SetAttribute("SquareL", UDim2.fromOffset(200, 200))

-- Link the sheet to this ScreenGui so its rules apply here
local styleLink = Instance.new("StyleLink")
styleLink.StyleSheet = sheet
styleLink.Parent = screenGui

-- A rule that targets every Frame (class selector)
local rule = Instance.new("StyleRule")
rule.Selector = "Frame"
rule.Parent = sheet
rule:SetProperties({
	BackgroundColor3 = "$Magenta", -- use the token
	Size = "$SquareL",
	BorderSizePixel = 0,
})

-- Any Frame we add now gets the style automatically
local frame = Instance.new("Frame")
frame.Parent = screenGui
explain: We make a `StyleSheet` and store it in ReplicatedStorage.
We add two tokens as attributes: a magenta color and a 200 by 200 pixel size.
A `StyleLink` inside the ScreenGui connects the sheet to this ScreenGui and everything in it.
The `StyleRule` with selector `"Frame"` matches every Frame. Its properties use the tokens with `$`.
When we add a new Frame, it turns magenta and 200 by 200 without us setting those properties on it.

watchOut: Forgetting the `StyleLink`. Without it, your rules never reach the UI. Put it inside the ScreenGui and set its `StyleSheet`.
Expecting the Properties window to show the styled value. It still shows the default; look for the warning mark and hover it.
Tag selectors need the dot: write `".ButtonPrimary"`, not `"ButtonPrimary"`, and remember to actually tag the object.
Themes that are meant to swap must define the same token names, or some looks will break when you switch.
Setting a property by hand on an object overrides the style. If an object will not follow your rule, check for a bold value and reset it.
